description.narrative: Projektets mål är (a) att stödja nationalförsamlingens institutionella kapacitet och strategiska kommunikation och rikta in sig på oberoende organ (revisionskammaren och Human Rights Defender's Office) för att driva framåt den moderna offentliga politiska agendan och förbättra utförandet av dess kärnfunktioner; (b) stärka den relevanta kompetensen hos parlamentsledamöterna och personalen i nationalförsamlingen.

The objectives of the Project are (a) supporting the institutional capacities and strategic communication of the National Assembly and target independent bodies (Chamber of Audit and Human Rights Defender's Office) to drive forward the modern public policy agenda and improve performance of its core functions; (b) enhancing the relevant competencies of the MPs and the staff of the National Assembly.

The project will aim at supporting the institutional capacities and strategic communication and collaboration of the National Assembly and target independent bodies (Chamber of Audit and Ombudsperson) to drive forward modern public policy agenda and improve performance of its core functions. It will enhance the relevant competencies of the MPs, and the staff of the National Assembly. The project is based on the previous cooperation with the NA and the respective lessons learned. The project efforts will focus on enhancing the institutional capacity of the National Assembly to fulfill its constitutional duties in more inclusive, responsive, transparent, accountable, and effective way, including, in engaging with citizens, civil society and public sector.
Outcome: The National Assembly is more inclusive, responsive, transparent, accountable and effective.
Result 1. Strategic vision of the National Assembly and roadmap for reforms, strategic communication and collaboration are consolidated empowering modern public policy agenda and fostering inclusive practices.
Result 2. The National Assembly is equipped with state-of-the-art methods and instruments for effectively pursuing its modern public policy agenda and improving performance of its core functions.
Result 3. Competencies of the MPs and the staff of the National Assembly in utilizing innovative methods, using and producing knowledge products towards advancing the modern public policy agenda and enhancing effectiveness of their core functions strengthened.
The project will design and introduce digitalised solutions to streamline functions and processes of the independent bodies, and facilitate collaboration with the National Assembly. It will build the capacities of the members and the target staff of the Audit Chamber and Ombudsperson office to enable them to engage with the modern public policy agenda, enhance the oversight function and promote rights-based approach to public policy making respectively, through applying new competencies of effective communication and stakeholder engagement.

Output 1
- Institutional needs assessment across all National Assembly (NA) departments conducted - Approval and launch of the NA Strategic Vision, Reform Strategy, Roadmap, Action Plan, and Communication Plan - 3 NA Standing Committee (SC on Financial-Credit and Budgetary Affairs, SC on Human Rights and Public Affairs, and SC on State and Legal Affairs) pilot Action Plans aligned with NA Reform Strategy templates - Joint reform consultations with NA staff, OECD/SIGMA, and UNDP on parliamentary service regulations - Expanded civic education through the NA Parliamentary Democracy Center - Parliamentary Democracy Center Strategy Addendum and Action Plan developed, validated with NA staff - An analytical study on the rights of refugees from Nagorno-Karabakh conducted - Dialogue platforms on modern public policy addressing displacement and inclusion - Regional consultations, focus groups, and feedback sessions to validate findings and refine policy recommendations - Revision of the NA Gender Equality Plan (GE) and transformation of the revision into GE and Social Inclusion (GESI) Plan - Introduction of NA GESI and Human Rights mainstreaming tools for pre-legislative scrutiny - Trainings on social inequalities and inclusive policy-making for MPs and staff - Progress toward establishing a NA GESI Council/Caucus (methodological guidelines and Charter of the Caucus developed) - Standing Committee on State and Legal Affairs advanced drafting of a Code of Conduct for MPs based on project advised model and framework for establishing a permanent Ethics Committee, aligned with GRECO recommendations. - Audit Chamber (AC) received targeted technical assistance in human resources management, recruitment processes, and institutional communications. - Audit Chambers new website and institutional branding completed.
Output 2
- Prolonging the Speech-to-Text software licenses with AI possible addition - Added new platform within the e-Parliament: "Parliament in Figures statistical indicators and webpage was developed to enhance transparency and public engagement - Introduction of eMonitor tool for hate speech and disinformation monitoring - Digitalizing VHS and other archival tape formats were initiated to safeguard historical recordings and ensure long-term accessibility - Equipped and upgraded conference system of the NA - A climate change e-Module for the parliamentarians
Output 3
- Capacity development package was delivered to MPs, party representatives, and NA staff, including a full-cycle Power BI data visualization training for 14 NA staff (3 men, 11 women) from key Standing Committees and support units. - Transformative Leadership Workshop for MPs and party representatives; cybersecurity awareness training for NA staff. - AI governance and ethics workshop series jointly delivered by UNDPs Chief Digital Office and the Democratic Institutions and Processes Team. - AI Empowerment for Parliamentary Staff training on practical AI applications for research, drafting support, transcription, and idea generation. - Peer-to-peer learning for MPs, NA staff, and AC including a study visit to UK Parliament focusing on faction formation, ethical governance, financial oversight, and parliamentary operational best practices. - International training course on organization of parliamentary work, jointly organized by the NA and the Senate for French-speaking parliamentarians and civil servants. - Participation of a woman MP, NA Staff and UNDP personnel in the UN Global Leadership Academy: Women Leading in the - Digital Era resulted in drafting a National Rollout Plan for Armenia. - International parliamentary conference on Role of Parliament in Shaping the Future of Responsible AI, jointly organized by Parliament of Malaysia, Inter-Parliamentary Union, Canadian Parliamentary Association, and UNDP.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
